discovery: Discovery of the two-dimensional electron system at oxide heterointerfaces (LaAlO3/SrTiO3) and its emergent electronic phases

nominees.name: Harold Y. Hwang
nominees.affiliation: Stanford University and SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory, USA

nominees.name: Jochen Mannhart
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: correlated oxide interfaces
motivation: In 2004 Ohtomo and Hwang showed that joining two band insulators, LaAlO3 and SrTiO3, with atomic-layer precision creates a high-mobility two-dimensional electron system at their interface. Mannhart and co-workers then showed that this interface has a critical thickness, that its conductivity can be switched by electric fields, and that it becomes superconducting. Together these results established that an interface between oxides can act as a new material, with phases that neither parent compound has, including gate-tunable superconductivity, magnetism and strong Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The work started the worldwide field of oxide interface engineering and changed how physicists design correlated quantum matter: atom by atom, using polar discontinuities, strain and symmetry breaking. It led directly to oxide electronics, interface superconductivity and Hwang's later discovery of nickelate superconductivity in thin films. It is a rare case of a discovery that created an entire research discipline.
